cylinder_block.name: Cylinder Block
cylinder_block.description: The main body of the engine. It holds the cylinders the pistons move in, and supports the crankshaft at the bottom.
facts: Usually cast from iron or aluminium alloy.
Contains passages (water jackets) for coolant and galleries for oil.
In an inline-4 all four cylinders sit in one straight row.
Shown cut away here so the moving parts in front of it are visible.

cylinder_head.name: Cylinder Head
cylinder_head.description: Bolted on top of the block, it closes the top of each cylinder and holds the valves, spark plugs and usually the camshaft.
facts: Forms the top of the combustion chamber.
A head gasket seals it to the cylinder block.
Contains the intake and exhaust ports that the valves open and close.

pistons.name: Pistons
pistons.description: Cylindrical parts that slide up and down inside the cylinders. Burning fuel pushes them down, and that force is passed to the crankshaft.
facts: Usually made of aluminium alloy to keep them light.
Piston rings seal the gap between piston and cylinder wall.
In a four-stroke engine each piston goes through intake, compression, power and exhaust strokes.
In an inline-4, pistons 1 and 4 move together, as do 2 and 3, which is why two are shown up and two down.

connecting_rods.name: Connecting Rods
connecting_rods.description: Rods that link each piston to the crankshaft, turning the piston's up-and-down motion into the crankshaft's rotation.
facts: The small end connects to the piston via a wrist (gudgeon) pin.
The big end wraps around a crankpin on the crankshaft, with a bearing between them.
Commonly made of forged steel.

crankshaft.name: Crankshaft
crankshaft.description: The rotating shaft at the bottom of the engine that turns the pistons' reciprocating motion into rotation that drives the wheels.
facts: Has offset crankpins (throws) where the connecting rods attach.
Turns twice for every full four-stroke cycle of each cylinder.
Drives the camshaft through the timing belt or chain at half its speed.
Supported in the block by main bearings.

camshaft.name: Camshaft
camshaft.description: A shaft with egg-shaped lobes that push the valves open at the right moment in each cycle.
facts: Turns at half the crankshaft's speed in a four-stroke engine.
Each lobe opens one valve (or a pair) as it rotates.
This model shows a single overhead camshaft (SOHC) layout.

intake_valves.name: Intake Valves
intake_valves.description: Valves that open to let the air-fuel mixture (or air, in direct-injection engines) into each cylinder during the intake stroke.
facts: Usually slightly larger than exhaust valves to help air flow in.
Held closed by valve springs and pushed open by the camshaft.
This model shows one intake valve per cylinder; many engines use two.

exhaust_valves.name: Exhaust Valves
exhaust_valves.description: Valves that open to let burnt gases out of each cylinder during the exhaust stroke.
facts: They run much hotter than intake valves.
Often made from heat-resistant steel alloys.
Opened by the camshaft and closed by valve springs.

spark_plugs.name: Spark Plugs
spark_plugs.description: Devices that make a spark inside each cylinder to ignite the compressed air-fuel mixture in a petrol engine.
facts: The spark jumps a small gap between two electrodes.
A ceramic insulator keeps the high voltage from leaking to the engine.
They fire near the end of the compression stroke.
Diesel engines do not use spark plugs; they rely on compression heat.

flywheel.name: Flywheel
flywheel.description: A heavy disc on the end of the crankshaft that smooths out the engine's pulses of power and connects to the clutch or torque converter.
facts: Stores rotational energy between power strokes.
Its outer ring gear is turned by the starter motor to start the engine.
In manual cars the clutch presses against it.

timing_belt.name: Timing Belt
timing_belt.description: A toothed belt that links the crankshaft to the camshaft so the valves open in step with the pistons.
facts: Keeps the camshaft turning at exactly half crankshaft speed.
Some engines use a metal timing chain instead of a belt.
Belts are replaced at intervals set by the manufacturer; a snapped belt can damage an interference engine.

oil_pan.name: Oil Pan
oil_pan.description: The tray bolted to the bottom of the engine that holds the engine oil (the sump).
facts: The oil pump draws oil from here and sends it around the engine.
Has a drain plug used during oil changes.
Also called the sump.
